diagnostic_evidence.quote: the sequence \( \{U_h^n(\mathbf{x})\}_{n=0}^{N}\subset H_0(\Omega)\) is called a set of SLDG numerical solutions
The field function \(u(x, t)\) to be solved is approximated by a \(P\)-th order DG polynomial

issues.failure_explanation: Prose claims: existence, uniqueness and stability of the CSLDG numerical solution are established. What is established: Definition def-NumSol-SLDG requires only that the sequence lie in H_0(Omega) and satisfy eq-discrete-SLDG for ALL test functions Psi in H_0(Omega_K); no DG polynomial space is imposed on the solution or tests anywhere in Section 3. For this system the Riesz argument yields, per element, a general L2 representer (multiplied by chi_{Omega_K}), which is precisely the exact characteristic transport of the previous iterate; the 'numerical solution' is the exact solution of the transport problem, with no discretization. The scheme actually computed (1D-SLDG-A1/A2 and the tensor-product scheme) matches only the orthonormal moments, i.e., applies the L2 projection onto polynomials, an object for which Theorems thm-NumericalScheme-Existence, thm-NumericalSolution-Stability and thm-NumericalSolution-Uniqueness prove nothing. The difference between the advertised analysis of the SLDG scheme and the delivered analysis of the unprojected variational problem is the defect.

failure_location.quote: First, the existence and uniqueness of the CSLDG numerical solutions are proven, along with the stability of the numerical scheme.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the DG constraint to Definition def-NumSol-SLDG (solution in the span of the cell basis, tests only against that basis); existence becomes an immediate orthonormal moment matching, and the stability/uniqueness inductions carry over verbatim since the chosen test (difference of two polynomial solutions) is admissible. All advertised guarantees survive in comparable form.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised first-time existence, uniqueness and stability analysis of the CSLDG scheme is not delivered: Section 3's guarantees concern an object different from the polynomial scheme computed by the algorithms of Sections 2 and 4, so the abstract, introduction and conclusion overclaim.
issues.title: Well-posedness/stability results analyze an infinite-dimensional variational problem, not the SLDG (DG) scheme
issues.why_classification: The contained repair (restrict solution/test space to the DG space and rerun the same variational arguments) preserves every advertised guarantee for the actual scheme; more than a local edit, but no new proof architecture and no loss of results.

issues.failure_explanation: Both inclusions of the support identity are derived from the implication 'x in support implies the function value at x is nonzero' and its converse. For L^2 functions (and even for continuous ones) points of the support may carry value zero, so both inclusions as argued are invalid inferences; the argument also never uses the continuity of the characteristic map, which is what actually yields supp{psi(. , t*)} = Phi^{-1}(supp Psi). The statement is true, but the given proof does not establish it.

failure_location.quote: For all \(\mathbf{x}^* \in \operatorname{supp}\{\psi(\mathbf{x}, t^*)\}\), where \(t^* \in [t_1, t_2]\), we have \(\psi(\mathbf{x}^*, t^*) \neq 0\).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the pointwise nonzero implications by the continuity argument: the backflow map is a homeomorphism, so supp{psi(.,t*)} = closure{psi(. ,t*) != 0} = Phi^{-1}(closure{Psi != 0}) = Phi^{-1}(supp Psi), which equals the displayed set and CODE_{t2->t*}(Omega); a short local rewrite.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma 3.1 is unproven as written; the support facts invoked later (e.g., supp{psi^0} in the existence proof) rest on an unsound argument, although the facts themselves are standard.
issues.title: Support lemma proved via invalid pointwise-nonzero inferences
issues.why_classification: A short local rewrite of two implications restores the proof; the lemma's statement and all downstream uses survive unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Note that once \(t_1\) and \(t_2\) are fixed, \(\int_{t_1}^{t_2} \mathbf{A}(\mathbf{s}(\tau), \tau) \, \mathrm{d}\tau\) is a constant.

The vector function \( \mathbf{A}(\mathbf{x},t) = (a_1(\mathbf{x},t), a_2(\mathbf{x},t), \ldots, a_d(\mathbf{x},t))^{\text{T}} \) is assumed to be continuous with respect to both \( \mathbf{x} \) and \( t \), and its first-order partial derivatives are also continuous.

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma lemma-psi-Rd-LP and Lemma lemma-psi-Omega-LP claim exact L^P-norm preservation under the characteristic map. Both proofs perform the substitution y = x + int A ds and treat the displacement as a constant independent of the starting point ('the domain of integration remains unchanged'; 'int A ds is a constant', so its x*-derivative is 0). But s(tau) is the characteristic through the starting point, so the displacement depends on x: the substitution is the flow map Phi, whose Jacobian determinant is not identically 1 unless the flow preserves Lebesgue measure, a hypothesis never imposed on A (only C^1 regularity is assumed). Counterexample: A(x,t) = x in 1D gives psi(x,t1) = Psi(x e^{t2-t1}), so the L1 norm is scaled by e^{-(t2-t1)} and the claimed equality fails. Consequently Lemma-f-H*'s boundedness step (which additionally equates norms over G and over the image CODE(G)) and the equalities ||psi^0|| = ||Psi|| used in the stability proof are invalid as written.

failure_location.quote: Considering the \(L^P\)-norm over the entire space \(\mathbb{R}^d\), the domain of integration remains unchanged as \(\mathbb{R}^d\) before and after the change of variables. Thus, we immediately obtain

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace each claimed equality by the change-of-variables identity int_G |W(Phi(x))|^P dx = int_{Phi(G)} |Psi|^P |det D Phi^{-1}| dy and bound the Jacobian on the compactly swept region (finite for C^1 A over finite time); weaken Lemmas 3.2/3.3 from equality to inequality and let the per-step constants C_k in the stability proof absorb the factors. No theorem statement needs to change.
issues.overall_effect: Lemmas 3.2 and 3.3 are false for general (compressible) velocity fields; the boundedness argument of Lemma Lemma-f-H* and the norm-preservation steps in the proofs of Theorems thm-NumericalScheme-Existence and thm-NumericalSolution-Stability, and hence the uniqueness argument built on stability, are unsound as written. The theorem statements can be retained with constants absorbing the flow Jacobian.
issues.title: Characteristic change of variables drops the flow Jacobian: L^P-norm-invariance lemmas are false
issues.why_classification: The repair is a standard, contained change-of-variables estimate replacing a false isometry; all theorem statements survive in the same form (the stability constant C is unspecified anyway), so no advertised guarantee or regime is lost, but several estimates must be re-derived, which exceeds a routine local fix.
